description: AstroNova is a team of students passionate about space, technology, and innovation. We’re excited to work together and build a creative solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We welcome teammates interested in coding, AI/ML, game development, design, data, space science, and storytelling. Most importantly, we value creativity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn.
summary: MissionForge is a space mission design game created by Team AstroNova for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We wanted to make space exploration more interesting and enjoyable by turning the idea of designing a space mission into an interactive gaming experience. Through MissionForge, players can explore the exciting world of space missions while learning about the creativity and challenges behind space exploration. Our goal is to bring space science closer to people, inspire curiosity, and show that learning about the universe can be both fun and engaging.
details:
MISSIONFORGE – Space Mission Design Game

About the Project

MISSIONFORGE turns spacecraft engineering into an interactive game where players can experience the challenges of planning and designing a space mission. Instead of simply reading about space engineering, players get to make decisions, explore different possibilities, and see how their choices affect the mission.

Our idea was simple: what if anyone could experience the role of a mission director and discover how exciting space engineering can be?

The Problem

Real space missions involve many connected engineering challenges. A spacecraft must stay within mass and budget limits, generate enough power, communicate with Earth despite signal delays, survive extreme temperatures, and follow a feasible trajectory. Every decision affects other parts of the mission.

For many students, these concepts remain abstract because they rarely get the opportunity to experiment with them. Space engineering can therefore feel complex and difficult to explore without specialized knowledge or equipment.

Our Solution

MISSIONFORGE brings these challenges into an interactive, browser-based gaming experience. Players design their own spacecraft, select scientific instruments, configure essential systems, plan trajectories, and prepare their missions for launch.

Every engineering decision comes with consequences. Players can discover what works, understand what goes wrong, and learn why different choices matter. The game is accessible directly through a web browser, without requiring installation or special hardware.

How MISSIONFORGE Works

The experience follows the journey of planning and executing a space mission:

  1. Mission Brief: Players choose from Lunar Polar Exploration, Mars Surface Science, Asteroid Survey, or Earth Climate Orbit.
  2. Destination Explorer: An interactive 3D solar system introduces destinations, environmental conditions, and communication delays.
  3. Spacecraft Builder: Players select a small, medium, or heavy spacecraft chassis inside a live 3D hangar.
  4. Scientific Payload: Instruments such as cameras, radar, spectrometers, and sensors are selected within mass, power, and budget limits.
  5. Launch Vehicle: Players choose a rocket, while the game checks payload capacity and compatibility.
  6. Spacecraft Subsystems: Power, communications, propulsion, and thermal-control systems are configured to support the mission.
  7. Trajectory Planning: Players compare fast, balanced Hohmann-style, and fuel-efficient transfer options.
  8. Flight Readiness Review: A PASS, WARNING, or FAIL checklist evaluates mission readiness. Critical failures prevent launch and explain what needs to be fixed.
  9. Launch and Simulation: Players experience an animated launch, telemetry, mission events, and interactive segments such as ascent, cockpit views, and planetary landing.
  10. Mission Results: A scored debrief highlights strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations, with an option to print the report.

For first-time players and judges, a one-click Demo Mission provides a quick way to experience a complete mission. An in-game assistant also helps explain technical terms and failed readiness checks.

The Science Behind the Game

MISSIONFORGE uses simplified educational models to introduce important spacecraft engineering concepts. These include mass and power budgets, inverse-square solar power, signal delay based on the speed of light, the rocket equation for delta-v and propellant, Hohmann-style transfers, and thermal-control constraints.

We clearly distinguish educational simplifications from precise engineering calculations. Values without documented sources are treated as illustrative rather than authoritative scientific measurements.

How We Built It

Our team used AI-assisted development tools to support different stages of the project.

  • Claude (Anthropic): Supported requirement documents, developer guides, workflow diagrams, presentation content, documentation, and discovery of candidate public NASA datasets.
  • Google Antigravity: Supported code generation and refactoring during development.

AI-assisted source files include comments identifying AI assistance and team review. Team AstroNova remains responsible for reviewing the generated code and project content.

NASA datasets listed in docs/NASA_DATA_SOURCES.md were identified through public NASA catalogs. Dataset values are used as simplified educational parameters unless their sources and units are explicitly documented.

Why MISSIONFORGE Matters

We believe learning about space should be more than memorizing facts. MISSIONFORGE allows students to experiment with mission decisions, understand engineering trade-offs, and learn from their own mistakes.

The project aims to:

  • Make space engineering more approachable through hands-on learning.
  • Encourage curiosity, creativity, and problem-solving.
  • Help students understand the relationship between mass, power, cost, and mission risk.
  • Make space education accessible through a free, browser-based experience.
  • Promote transparency by explaining engineering rules and documenting data sources.

What Comes Next

MISSIONFORGE is an evolving project, and we see many opportunities to expand it. Our future plans include a more complete launch and interplanetary flight experience, planetary landing, multi-planet exploration, and Earth-return missions.

We also hope to introduce saved missions, more documented NASA scientific datasets, improved spacecraft and planetary visuals, an AI-driven mission guidance system, and a classroom mode with Bengali language support.

Our long-term vision is to make MISSIONFORGE a learning experience where students can explore space missions, understand the science behind them, and feel inspired to imagine their own future in space exploration.
